# Encode / Decode

[← All actions](README.md)

Encodes or decodes one value: Base64, Base64URL, URL, XML / HTML / JSON escape, Quoted-Printable, RFC 2047 or RegEx escape.

| | |
|---|---|
| Enum name | `EncodeDecode` |
| Ordinal | `"action": 5564431` |
| Category | Data |
| Terminating | `false` |
| Group / edges | No |
| Availability | GA |

## What it does

The step resolves the SmartText `input`, converts it with the chosen `format` in the chosen `direction`, and writes the text to the output `result`. Text is UTF-8 in both directions; only RFC 2047 encoded words carry their own character set.

| `format` | encode | decode |
|---|---|---|
| `base64` | UTF-8 bytes as standard base64 with padding | base64 to UTF-8 text; spaces and line breaks are ignored |
| `base64url` | URL alphabet (`-` and `_`), no padding | the same, padding is restored |
| `urlForm` | percent-encoding, space as `+` | `+` becomes a space, `%XX` is decoded |
| `urlPath` | percent-encoding, space as `%20` | `%XX` is decoded, `+` stays |
| `xml` | `& < > " '` as entities | named XML entities and numeric entities |
| `html` | like `xml`, `'` as `&#39;` | additionally the named HTML 4 / Latin-1 entities (`&nbsp;`, `&auml;`, `&euro;`, `&ndash;`, …) |
| `json` | escapes `" \` and control characters (no surrounding quotes) | `\" \\ \/ \b \f \n \r \t \uXXXX`; an unescaped `"` is invalid |
| `quotedPrintable` | RFC 2045, `=XX`, soft line breaks at 76 characters | removes soft line breaks, `=XX` bytes as UTF-8 |
| `rfc2047` | unchanged if printable ASCII, else `=?utf-8?B?…?=` words | decodes every `B` / `Q` encoded word in the text |
| `regex` | escapes regex metacharacters | – (not allowed) |

An empty resolved input gives an empty `result`. Invalid input in decode direction fails the step.

## Configuration

| key | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `direction` | string | no | `"decode"` | `"encode"` or `"decode"`, case-insensitive. A missing value means decode; any other value fails the step. |
| `format` | string | no | `"base64"` | One of the codes in the table above, case-insensitive. A missing value means base64; any other value fails the step. |
| `input` | string | yes | – | The value to convert, usually a SmartField such as `"{{GetAttachments_contentBytes}}"`. SmartText. |

## Outputs

| name | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `result` | value | always; the converted text. Values of several hundred KB are stored completely. |

## Validation

| stage | severity | rule | message |
|---|---|---|---|
| publish | warning | `direction` is not `encode` / `decode` | `Encode / Decode step '%1': Direction '%2' is unknown. Use encode or decode.` |
| publish | warning | `format` is not a known code | `Encode / Decode step '%1': Format '%2' is unknown. Use base64, base64url, urlForm, urlPath, xml, html, json, quotedPrintable, rfc2047 or regex.` |
| publish | warning | `format` `regex` with `direction` `decode` | `Encode / Decode step '%1': RegEx escape can only encode. Use the direction Encode.` |
| publish | warning | `input` is empty or missing | `Encode / Decode step '%1': Enter the input to encode or decode.` |
| editor | error | direction, format or input is empty (required fields) | `Please fill in the highlighted fields.` |

`%1` is the step **id**, not its description.

## Runtime errors

| condition | message |
|---|---|
| Unknown `direction` | `Direction '%1' is unknown. Use encode or decode.` |
| Unknown `format` | `Format '%1' is unknown. Use base64, base64url, urlForm, urlPath, xml, html, json, quotedPrintable, rfc2047 or regex.` |
| `regex` with `decode` | `RegEx escape can only encode. Use the direction Encode.` |
| Decode input is not valid in the format (`%1` = `Base64`, `Base64URL`, `JSON-escaped text`, `Quoted-Printable`, `RFC 2047 encoded word`) | `The input is not valid %1.` |
| RFC 2047 word with another character set than UTF-8, ISO-8859-1, Windows-1252, US-ASCII | `The character set %1 is not supported in RFC 2047 encoded words. Supported are UTF-8, ISO-8859-1, Windows-1252 and US-ASCII.` |

## Reading attachments of S/MIME signed mails (Microsoft Graph)

For a signed mail, Graph `/messages/{id}/attachments` returns one attachment `smime.p7m` with `contentType` `multipart/signed`; its `contentBytes` hold the whole MIME message. The attachments inside are not listed separately.

1. **Encode / Decode** `decode` + `base64` on `contentBytes` → the MIME message as text.
2. **Parser** `RegEx`, line `part`: `(?s)(Content-Type:(?:(?!\r\n\r\n).)*?Content-Disposition:\s*attachment.*?)(?=\r?\n--)` → one value per attachment part (`part[0]`, `part[1]`, …).
3. **For Each** over the parts, then **Parser** `RegEx` with the lines `fileName` `filename\*?="?([^"\r\n;]+)`, `contentType` `Content-Type:\s*([^;\r\n]+)`, `encoding` `Content-Transfer-Encoding:\s*(\S+)`, `body` `(?s)\r?\n\r?\n(.*)`.
4. **Encode / Decode** `decode` + `rfc2047` on `fileName`. Skip `smime.p7s` (the signature). A `base64` body is the file content as base64 already; decode a `quoted-printable` body with `quotedPrintable`.

To use a boundary inside a regular expression, escape it first with `encode` + `regex`.

## Gotchas

- Base64 decode returns **text**. Decoding binary content (PDF, images) to text loses data. Keep binary content as base64.
- Quoted-Printable decode always reads the bytes as UTF-8; ISO-8859-1 content shows wrong umlauts.
- The RegEx template above is no full MIME parser: folded headers in another order, `filename*=` (RFC 2231), forwarded mails (`message/rfc822`) and encrypted S/MIME (`application/pkcs7-mime`) are not or only partly covered.
- `json` escapes only the content; add the surrounding quotes yourself when building JSON text.
- The Debug execution log contains the input and the result.
